ambient_events: The Robo Teller's servos whir as it rotates a precise eleven degrees to face the next nobody.
A woman at the far ATM counts a withdrawal twice, folds it small, and puts it somewhere unpleasant.
The floor guard's coat shifts. Something under it shifts with a different weight.
Footsteps come back off the marble twice: once for you, once a half-second late.
The camera in the cornice tracks a slow arc across the hall and settles, briefly, on you.
A cleaning drone works a single square metre of floor to a mirror shine and moves on to the next.
Somewhere behind the wall, machinery that isn't an elevator moves something heavy.
The air handling comes on with a sigh. It smells of stone dust and money that has been counted many times.
description: A hall built to make people feel small, and it works. Veined white marble goes up the walls to a coffered ceiling four storeys overhead, and every sound you make comes back at you a half-second later, cleaner. There are no chairs. There is nowhere to wait, because Citadel does not want you to wait; it wants you to transact and leave. Two cash terminals sit recessed in stone alcoves, their orange fascias the only colour in the room. At the far end, behind a marble counter with no gap in it anywhere, a chest-high machine of enamel and brushed steel swivels to face whoever comes through the doors. A guard in a charcoal coat stands where the floor is worn faintly grey, which tells you how many years he has stood exactly there. Beyond him the marble stops and a slab of armoured steel begins.

window.description: A window set too high in the wall to see the ground through, so it offers the sky and nothing else. On a bad day that is more information than you want.
window.name: the high window

name: Citadel Financial — The Marble Hall
